assessment.headline: DAY 35. Good Friday. UN votes on Hormuz. India joins coalition. Brent $109. Three days to the deadline.
assessment.body:
Three converging events make today critical even though markets are closed:

1. UN SECURITY COUNCIL VOTES on Bahrain's Hormuz resolution — 'all defensive means necessary' to secure the strait. 136 co-sponsors. But China and Russia will likely veto, calling it 'legitimizing force.' If vetoed, there is NO international legal framework to reopen Hormuz.

2. INDIA JOINED THE COALITION. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri participated in UK-led 60+ nation talks on Hormuz. India is also supplying oil to Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka — and Maldives has formally requested fuel. India is emerging as the region's energy stabilizer.

3. BRENT SURGED TO $109 — up 7.78% since Trump's 'stone ages' speech. Russian Urals crude at $123.45. The market is saying: this war is not ending. Dry bulk through Hormuz collapsed 83%.

Overnight: Tehran-Karaj bridge collapsed (8 dead, 95 wounded). Ballistic missile chief Atimi killed. AWS data centers in Bahrain struck. China banned jet fuel exports. Korean Air in emergency mode. Philippines considering grounding planes.

India snapshot (Day 35):
• 60 days fuel stock. LPG 30+ days. Refineries >100%. 800 TMT cargoes secured
• Rupee 93.19 (recovered from 94.84 on RBI NDF ban)
• Sensex 73,320 (most volatile day yesterday: -1,584 → +185)
• FII ₹1.23T March + ₹8,331 Cr Apr 1
• India supplying oil to 5 neighboring countries
• Manufacturing PMI at 4-year low
• Markets reopen MONDAY — the same day as April 6 deadline

The Al Jazeera analysis is the most important thing for Indians to understand: even if Hormuz reopens TOMORROW, the disruption lasts MONTHS. Hundreds of ships need to transit. Insurance premiums are permanent. Iran's toll system is permanent. Congestion will be massive. The pre-war world of free, easy Hormuz passage is permanently over. India must plan for a structurally higher energy cost future.
